items.title: Steve Buckingham, interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 25, 2019 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Some guys got so busy, especially in LA, like Larry Carlton, they started charging triple scale to try to discourage the sessions, but they still got hired.

ctx.x: Yeah. The good ones and the bad ones. Well yeah, there were days you showed up and it was just routine but you had to be professional like I was going to say, and it was the task

at hand. You walk in, you hear the demo, they either handed you a chart or you wrote your own chart, and you would run it down one time. If there were mistakes, make your notes what you were supposed to do. And then you would usually get it, and me as a producer too, but the players I’d work with, you’d get it in usually the first, second or third take. You had to. If it took longer than that then you’re running — sessions are divided into three hour segments, usually 10 in the morning to 1, one hour break, 2…

When you became a producer, and I’m thinking about people coming out of music schools and so forth, and they wanted to get into this whatever is left of the business — you assume that these musicians are good players but what else do they have to bring or not bring in order to keep getting hired again.
